notes:
Key context: enterprise search for regulated finance products. Heavy emphasis on retrieval + a second-stage neural reranker.
- Current infra: self-hosted vector DB (approx 50M short-form documents), nightly batch updates + nearline streaming.
- "We cannot accept any measurable drop in top-3 quality" — Head of Search on 2026-01-15 call.
- Outcome desired: migrate to new embeddings + lighter-weight reranker to cut per-query cost by ~30% without harming QA.
- Primary concerns: hidden regressions in corner-case queries, transient latency spikes during cache-warm, index build throughput.
- Evaluation approach agreed: automated evals (MRR, nDCG, recall@k) + human spot checks on 2k hard queries; A/B traffic split then canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) if no regressions.
- Pricing sensitivity: wants unit economics at p95 latency target; open to Dedicated or Private if predictable throughput and residency guarantees.
- Internal champions: Head of Search (Sasha V.), Senior ML Eng (Diego R.).
- Next week: Arjun to hand off an eval harness + seed prompts, Lina to schedule CSM onboarding once POC approved.
use_case_summary: RAG for enterprise document search: embedding migration + neural reranker replacement. Customer wants scale (50M docs), sub-400ms p95 latency, and 20-40% cost reduction per query. Primary deliverables: eval harness for automated + human checks, A/B canary rollout plan, throughput & cost modeling for Dedicated/Private options.
indexing_scale: ~50M documents (text snippets + metadata), ingest growth ~10%/month, nightly reindex and hourly deltas
latency_targets: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms for full pipeline (vec search + reranker), tail spikes must be <1s
cost_per_query: $0.006 - $0.015 (depends on embedding dim, reranker size, and batching); target is <$0.01 avg
evaluation_strategy: Evals-driven migration: baseline automated metrics (nDCG@10, MRR), curated hard-queries set, human pass/fail labeling, A/B holdback + gradual canary (5/25/100). Reject if top-3 degrade >1.5% on nDCG or regression on SLA latency.
procurement_notes: Procurement prefers enterprise contract (1yr) with SLA. Legal needs data residency confirmation for EU customers. Pricing ask: committed capacity discounts for Dedicated.
